Score a setup on labeled rows

score_setup.Rd

Runs decide() with a setup on inputs whose true answers you know, and scores the probabilities with the area under the ROC curve. Use it to compare candidate setups (descriptions, instructions, references) on the learning rows. A person or an agent reads the estimate of each setup and keeps the best.

Usage

score_setup(
  setup,
  text = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  truth,
  role = NULL,
  metric = "roc_auc",
  event = NULL,
  path = NULL
)

Arguments

setup

A setup from decision_setup() or read_setup() with one question.

text, image

The inputs, as in decide().

truth

A factor or character vector with the true answer of each input. It has the length of the inputs, and its values are answers of the question.

role

NULL (the default, no check), or a vector with one value per input: "learning", "calibration" or "test". score_setup() stops before any request when a value is "test": score the test rows one time, with evaluate_once().

metric

The metric. This release has "roc_auc" only. For another metric, compute it from the answers column of the result with yardstick.

event

The answer that counts as the event (the positive class) of the AUC. NULL (the default) gives "true" for a noul question and the second answer for a question with two answers (for c(normal = ..., defective = ...), "defective"). With three or more answers, event is required.

path

NULL, or a state file for decide() (see path in decide()). A new call with the same path sends only the inputs that the file does not hold.

Value

A one-row tibble:

  • metric and estimate: the metric and its value. estimate is NA with a warning when fewer than one row of each class remains.

  • n: the number of rows in the AUC.

  • calls: the number of requests that this call sent (0 for inputs read from path).

  • input_tokens: the sum of the input tokens.

  • cost: the sum of every cost that the provider reports (rows with an error included: the provider billed them), or NA when a row that used input tokens has no reported cost. It is 0 when no row reports a cost or input tokens.

  • seconds: the sum of the response times.

  • errors: the number of rows with an .error (for example a failed call, or an answer with a missing probability). They stay out of the AUC.

  • answers: a list column that holds the output of decide().

input_tokens, cost and seconds count every row, also the rows that come from the path file. So a new call with the same path can report tokens and a cost with calls = 0.

Details

The AUC uses the probabilities that decide() returns, so it is the AUC of the calibrated probabilities when the setup has a calibrator. It is the Mann-Whitney statistic of the probability of event, with average ranks for ties; it equals yardstick::roc_auc_vec(truth, prob, event_level = "second") when event is the second level of truth.

The function checks setup, metric, event, truth and role before it sends a request.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
quality <- question_choice("Is the part defective?", c(
  nominal = "A clean part.", defective = "A part with a defect."
))
setup <- decision_setup(decider_typesafe("jev-1.13.0"), list(q = quality))
score_setup(
  setup, text = c("Clean surface.", "Dark streak."),
  truth = c("nominal", "defective"), role = c("learning", "learning")
)
} # }
